definitions.gloss: to visit (a sick or injured person), to pay a sympathy call
definitions.explanation: To visit someone who is ill, injured, or has experienced misfortune, in order to offer comfort and support.

definitions.gloss: to strike, to hit, to befall
definitions.explanation: Used when a disaster, calamity, or blow strikes a person or place. Often appears in passive form (見舞われる).

examples.japanese: {入院|にゅういん}した{友人|ゆうじん}を{見舞|みま}う。
{花|はな}を{持|も}って{病院|びょういん}に{見舞|みま}いに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to visit at the hospital with flowers.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}が{退院|たいいん}するまで{毎日|まいにち}{見舞|みま}いに{通|かよ}った。
examples.english: I visited every day until my grandmother was discharged from the hospital.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}に{見舞|みま}われた。
examples.english: We were hit by a typhoon.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{大|おお}きな{地震|じしん}に{見舞|みま}われた。
examples.english: This region was struck by a major earthquake.

examples.japanese: {経済|けいざい}{危機|きき}に{見舞|みま}われた{国|くに}は、{復興|ふっこう}に{何年|なんねん}もかかった。
examples.english: The country struck by an economic crisis took many years to recover.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 is the original meaning and is often used as the noun {見舞|みま}い (a visit to a sick person, a get-well gift). Sense 2 appears almost exclusively in the passive form {見舞|みま}われる, typically with natural disasters or crises as the subject.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見舞|みま}いに{行|い}く: to go visit (a sick person)
- {見舞|みま}い{客|きゃく}: visitor (to a sick person)
- お{見舞|みま}い: get-well visit/gift (polite form)
- {災害|さいがい}に{見舞|みま}われる: to be struck by a disaster
- {不幸|ふこう}に{見舞|みま}われる: to be visited by misfortune
